rows.source: Arithmetic check: with ρ = 4ε and ε' = ε the Lean radius condition is 12ε + 3d/q < 1; paper (A26) 6ε + 2d/q < 1/2 is 12ε + 4d/q < 1, which implies it. ALMSS Corollary 70 (almss-journal.txt:2647).
rows.text: 1b compresses "Its nearest polynomial is no farther away from the received row, so it lies within ..." to "is therefore within", which hides the one place nearestness is used. Adopt 1b's block with that sentence restored: "... The received selected row is within $6\varepsilon+d/q$ of the corresponding row of $P$. Its nearest polynomial is no farther from the received row, so it lies within $12\varepsilon+2d/q<1-d/q$ of that polynomial row, by (A26). Separation forces identity; the same argument applies to the column. This uses the [crossing lemma with a supplied bivariate polynomial](https://github.com/troyjlee/tcs-formalizations/blob/a0ce13ed0fa264f051c1278e039596ce65557fa4/PCP/Algebraic/PointLineCrossing.lean#L246), which requires nearestness only at the selected crossing."

In all 17 of 1b's replacements no m remains in mathematics. 12 of the 17 are pure renames (cm->cb, m^c->b^c, m^i->b^i, d=m=h=s -> d=b=h=s); the other five (b0031, b0054, b0074, b0128, and b0065-area text) also carry separate wording edits judged in rows L-a, L-e and the sampling section. rows.text: Adopt the rename, with two conditions. (1) Near-clash: b0125, b0126 and b0130 define and use the label-count exponent $b_r(t)$, and the radix $b$ then appears in the same subsection (b0128-b0136, e.g. $Q^{2j+cb}C_1$ two lines after $C_r=2^{b_r(t)}$, and $2^{(8d+cb)t+(t+1)^3+3}$ right after $b_1(t)\le b_3(t)$). There is no mathematical ambiguity (one is a scalar, the other a subscripted function), but the same letter carries two meanings within ten lines. Either accept this knowingly or rename the count exponent in b0125, b0126, b0130 (three occurrences: lines 404, 407, 420), for example to $\beta_r(t)$. Other uses of b in that chapter are in different sections and do not meet the radix: $d_b$ (b0161-b0162), $b_0$ (b0174, b0176), Boolean literals $a,b,c$ (b0189-b0191), intercept $b$ (b0203, b0209; also the theorem constants $a,b,\ell$ in b0008). (2) 1a's replacements for b0031, b0054, b0074 and b0128 still write $m$, $cm$, $m^c$, $z^{jm^i}$; if any 1a text is chosen for those blocks it must be alpha-renamed too.
